assessor: RTS governed build assessment — Exhausted-AI Human Escalation Gate v1
rationale: K0 reduced equal-priority review load but still mapped many high-impact or high-causal findings to HUMAN_NOW even when discriminating probes, deterministic checks, evidence-acquisition paths or bounded defer conditions remained. Live revalidation of the same 76 findings showed 35 AI_CONTINUE / 41 WAIT_SAFE_DEFER / 0 HUMAN_NOW after second-pass escape-route verification. K1 therefore gates human escalation on knowledge-integrated exhaustion: DA, Counter-DA and probe results must be folded into a cumulative knowledge state, and human return is allowed only when that accumulated evidence cannot produce a defensible decision, new discriminating test/evidence route, or safe defer for a materially consequential residual choice.

assets.notes: Reuse K0 materiality dimensions, separate adversarial views and explicit problem-solving paths.
Reuse bounded/explicit execution philosophy; K1 itself does not execute probes.

gaps: No current layer requires accumulated DA/Counter-DA/probe knowledge to be reintegrated before deciding that AI work is exhausted.
No current layer requires explicit exhaustion evidence before HUMAN_NOW.
No current layer distinguishes a high-priority finding with a remaining probe from a true human decision dead-end.
No current layer treats defensible decision, further evidence acquisition, discriminating experiment and safe defer as explicit escape routes from human escalation.
No current layer requires an auditable handoff packet explaining why the residual decision cannot be reduced further by AI.

risks: A claimed experiment may be too vague to be genuinely discriminating.
The system may loop by repeatedly proposing equivalent probes and falsely appear to be learning.
Safe defer may be asserted without a bounded trigger or recheck condition.
Missing verification evidence may accidentally be treated as exhaustion.
Accumulated knowledge may be recorded but not actually used to shrink or reshape the remaining UNKNOWN.
Human counts may be reduced as a vanity metric instead of preserving material dead-ends.
